A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DoFlow research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic forecasting experiments, hydropower forecasting and anomaly detection, cancer-treatment predictions, and an empirical check of assumption A3.

after.justification: v2 retains original forecasting and application results and reports revised synthetic results and additional CRPS comparisons.

M1.justification: Both versions use recurrent history encoders, per-node CNFs trained by conditional flow matching, intervention clamping, and factual encoding followed by counterfactual decoding. v2 reconciles the flow-direction description with the existing loss and decoding equations and clarifies state updates. Its application-specific implementation details do not establish an algorithm redesign.

E1.justification: The named benchmarks remain, but two synthetic data-generating families change substantially. In v2 Appendix D, FC-Layer replaces its square-root noise interaction with exponential/tanh parent effects and additive noise, despite retaining the NLNA label. Chain replaces its square-root mechanism with noise-scaled autoregression. These revise the represented dynamics and non-additivity coverage.

E2.justification: Synthetic and hydropower comparisons retain GRU, TFT, TiDE, TSMixer, DeepVAR, and MQF2; cancer comparisons retain CRN, RMSN, and MSM. The new CRPS table compares DoFlow with already evaluated DeepVAR and MQF2. No new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: v2 adds CRPS evaluation and replaces copying earlier root trajectories with explicitly generated half-period-shifted interventions. v1 describes coefficients randomized across trials, whereas v2 specifies fixed coefficients. The reported hydropower DAG also changes beyond renumbering: an isolated auxiliary generator state is replaced by a turbine state influenced by both roots. These are reported setting changes; rerunning all comparisons is not established.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix E.1 and Table 2 empirically examine assumption A3 by comparing latent-history joint distributions against independent Gaussian references. v2 removes this entire diagnostic and its supporting interpretation, without a replacement analysis of the assumption underpinning counterfactual recovery.

E5.justification: The joint-MMD statistical diagnostic for A3 is removed. v2 also explicitly distinguishes counterfactual evaluation with one deterministic trajectory and deviations across 50 test batches. The retained forecasting tables continue using batch-based standard deviations and predictive intervals; no increase in training seeds or repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Many DoFlow RMSE and MMD entries change. For example, Table 1 replaces Tree additive counterfactual RMSE 0.65±0.10 with 0.11±0.02, and Table 6 replaces Chain additive counterfactual RMSE 0.69±0.15 with 0.30±0.06. v2 adds CRPS results and changes sampling time from 9.45s to 10.25s. Baseline scores and Tables 7–8 remain unchanged. Revised settings prevent treating these replacements as demonstrated same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal causal assumptions covering unconfoundedness, consistency, positivity, and no interference in Appendix B.1. Assumption 4.1 strengthens monotonicity to strict monotonicity and continuity. Proposition 3.1 and its derivation remove conditioning on sampled latent variables from the trajectory density. The principal recovery proposition, corollary, and proof strategy remain.

C1.justification: The principal forecasting, recovery, and anomaly-detection contributions remain. However, v2 strengthens novelty positioning from an underexplored direction to an explicit assertion that no general counterfactual time-series forecasting framework exists. The introduction also drops v1's additional change-point-detection claim.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 and Appendix B.1 explicitly discuss the known, correctly specified DAG requirement and failure of guarantees under hidden confounding, with proposed discovery and deconfounding extensions. v2 also clarifies anomaly scores as densities of generated forecasts conditioned on observed contexts.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and an implementation appendix specifying PyTorch/torchdiffeq, optimization, network dimensions, windowing, training, time features, and cancer-treatment encoders. It supplies detailed simulation coefficients and the anomaly decision rule: a normal-score tenth-percentile threshold sustained for five minutes. These substantially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 removes the counterfactual-explainability discussion and associated references while substantially expanding causal-flow and confounding positioning. Additions include Khemakhem et al., Javaloy et al., PO-Flow, constrained counterfactual dynamics forecasting by Liu et al., DeCaFlow, and Neural Causal Models. The relationship to existing temporal causal methods is also rewritten.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten, method explanations are expanded, and discussion and conclusion sections are revised. Appendices are reorganized around causal assumptions, CNF preliminaries, simulation definitions, implementation, and results. The title and author/affiliation presentation also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference typography and headers and substantially rearranges page composition and display placement. It removes the A3 diagnostic table, adds a CRPS table and a 50-node Chain forecast figure, and revises the hydropower graph and forecast display. Most other figures and tables are retained with resizing or relocation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves implementation disclosure, clarifies causal limitations, and corrects flow and density exposition. However, it removes the only empirical A3 check and changes synthetic mechanisms and intervention schedules while retaining baseline scores and replacing many DoFlow scores. The PDFs do not explain how the revised settings align with those retained comparisons. These unresolved empirical issues prevent a reliable net-quality judgment despite clear documentation gains.
